auth.title: Sign-in
auth.description: Identity providers (OpenID Connect) that people can sign in with. Each sign-in service has its own callback URL to register on the identity provider.
auth.providersDescription: When Creates accounts is on, anyone who can sign in to that identity provider and whose email has no account here yet gets one the first time they sign in. Keep it off for providers anyone can sign up at, such as Google or gitlab.com.
auth.autoCreateFor: Create accounts on first sign-in with {{name}}
auth.callbackCopyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the URL and copy it yourself.
auth.secretMissing: No client secret yet. It can't be turned on until one is saved.
auth.clientIdMissing: Not set yet. The service can't be turned on until a client ID is saved.
auth.notConnected: Hasn't connected successfully yet, so the number of affected accounts may be off. Press Test connection.
auth.insecureIssuer: This issuer uses plain http: tokens and claims travel unencrypted between Knotebook and the identity provider.
auth.testOk: Connection OK. The identity provider reports issuer {{issuer}}.
auth.testScope: Testing reads only the identity provider's configuration. It can't tell whether the client ID or secret is right.

warnings.client_secret_post_not_advertised: The identity provider doesn't list client_secret_post, which Knotebook uses to send the client secret. Sign-in may fail at the last step.
warnings.secret_undecryptable: The saved client secret can't be decrypted (APP_SECRET may have changed). Enter it again.
warnings.client_id_missing: No client ID yet. Add it with Edit before turning the service on.

auth.disableDescription: Accounts and their linked sign-ins are kept, but nobody can sign in with this service until it's turned back on. People who are already signed in stay signed in.
auth.impactLockedOut: Of those, with no other way to sign in: {{number}}
auth.impactUnresolved: This service hasn't connected successfully yet, so these numbers may be off.

access.title: Password sign-in and registration
access.registrationHelp: Anyone can create an account on the registration page with an email and a password. Whether a sign-in service creates accounts is set for each service below. Invitations created by an admin work either way.
access.registrationNoEffect: Has no effect while password sign-in is off.
access.passwordLoginHelp: When off, everyone — including admins — can only sign in through a sign-in service. Accounts not yet linked to one can link themselves by signing in for the first time through a sign-in service with the same email and entering their old password. Turning it off doesn't sign anyone out. While it's off, password reset links and invitations can't be created or used; unused ones work again if you turn it back on before they expire.
access.needProvider: Turn on at least one sign-in service first.
access.needAdminLink: Link a sign-in service in your own settings first.
access.forced: Password sign-in is forced on by the environment variable PASSWORD_LOGIN_FORCE_ENABLE. The Allow password sign-in setting below takes effect only after you remove that variable and restart.
access.usersWithoutSso: Accounts with no usable sign-in service: {{number}}

auth.impactActingAdminLockedOut: After turning this off, you won't be able to sign in through a sign-in service yourself.
auth.deleteDisabledHint: Turn it off before deleting it.
auth.deleteDescription: Linked sign-ins are kept: if you add a service with the same issuer again, those people can sign in with it again.
auth.deleteLegacyNote: This service uses the old callback URL (…/api/auth/oidc/callback). A service you add later gets its own callback URL, so the identity provider's settings would have to change.
auth.turnedOff: This sign-in service was turned off.

create.title: Add sign-in service
create.clientIdHint: Optional for now. Some identity providers, such as GitLab, give you a client ID only after you register a callback URL — you'll see this service's callback URL once it's added.
create.startsOff: New sign-in services start turned off, and don't create accounts on first sign-in. Test the connection, then turn it on.

steps.title: Finish setting it up
steps.scopes: Allow the scopes openid, email and profile.
steps.client: Make it a confidential client that sends its secret with client_secret_post.
steps.clientId: Copy its client ID (GitLab calls it Application ID), then enter it here with Edit.
steps.secret: Copy its client secret, then paste it here with Edit.
steps.finish: Back here, press Test connection, then turn the service on.

edit.title: Edit sign-in service
edit.description: Leave the client secret empty to keep the current one.
edit.secretPlaceholderSaved: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
edit.sortOrderInvalid: Display order must be a whole number from 0 to 100000.
edit.issuerChangeClearsSecret: Changing the issuer clears the saved client secret and turns this service off.
edit.issuerChangeClearsSecretOnly: Changing the issuer clears the saved client secret.
edit.issuerChangeTurnsOff: Changing the issuer turns this service off. Test it, then turn it back on.
edit.autoCreateConfirmTitle: Keep creating accounts after changing the issuer?
edit.autoCreateConfirmDescription: {{name}} creates accounts on first sign-in. With the new issuer, anyone who can sign in to that identity provider and whose email has no account here yet will get one. Turn it off unless only your people can sign in there.

icon.title: Sign-in service icon
icon.description: Shown before this service's name on the sign-in buttons and lists.
icon.uploadHint: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 5 MB; it's resized to 128 px.
icon.unsupportedType: Only PNG, JPEG and WebP images are accepted.
icon.tooLarge: The image must be 5 MB or smaller.

validation.displayNameTooLong: Display name can be at most 40 characters.
validation.issuerScheme: Issuer URL must start with lowercase http:// or https://.
validation.issuerTooLong: Issuer URL can be at most 512 characters.
validation.issuerCredentials: Issuer URL can't contain a username or password.
validation.clientIdTooLong: Client ID can be at most 512 characters.
validation.secretBlank: Client secret can't be only spaces.
validation.secretTooLong: Client secret can be at most 4096 characters.
validation.unstorable: Contains characters that can't be saved.

admin.title: User management
admin.description: Invite people, grant admin rights, reset passwords, and disable people who have left.

passwordReset.title: Reset password
passwordReset.description: Creates a one-time link for {{email}} to set a new password. Their current password keeps working until the link is used; then their other browsers are signed out. API tokens and connected apps keep working.
passwordReset.pending: An unused link expires {{when}}. Creating a new one cancels it.
passwordReset.pendingSuspended: An unused link expires {{when}}. It can't be used while password sign-in is off.
passwordReset.passwordLoginOff: Password sign-in is off on this site, so password reset links can't be created or used.

oneTimeLink.onceWarning: Copy this link now — it won't be shown again. It works once and expires {{when}}.
oneTimeLink.copyFailed: Couldn't copy automatically — select the link above and copy it by hand.

invites.createDescription: Creates a one-time link someone can use to create their own account with an email and a password. Accounts created this way are regular users. Anyone who has the link can use it, with any email — send it only to the person you're inviting.
invites.passwordLoginOff: Password sign-in is off on this site, so invitations can't be created or used.
invites.labelHint: Only admins see it, in the invitations list. Up to 100 characters.
invites.labelTooLong: A note can be at most 100 characters.
invites.title: Invitations
invites.tableDescription: Invitations that were used, revoked or expired are removed from this list after 30 days.
invites.suspendedNotice: Password sign-in is off, so unused invitations can't be used right now. Turn it back on and the ones that haven't expired work again.
invites.revokeDescription: The link stops working right away. This can't be undone; create a new invitation if you need one.

admin.disableDescription: {{email}} will be signed out immediately and lose access until re-enabled.

storage.title: Storage plans
storage.description: A plan limits the total size of the attachments in a personal space or a group. New users and new groups start on the defaults below; changing a default doesn't move anyone who already exists.
storage.lowerNotice: Lowering the limit doesn't delete any files; spaces already over the new limit can't add attachments after this.
storage.quotaInvalid: Enter a size from 0 up to 1048576 GB.
storage.deleteDescription: {{name}} will be removed. This can't be undone.
storage.deleteBlockedHint: A plan that is a default, or that any user or group is on, can't be deleted.
storage.defaultsDescription: The plan newly created users and groups start on.

versions.title: Version history
versions.autoDescription: When off, no space saves versions automatically; people can still save versions by hand. Versions and note text don't count toward storage; quotas count uploaded files only.
versions.retentionDescription: All automatic versions from the last {{keepAll}} days are kept; up to {{dailyUntil}} days, one a day; older, one a week. Days and weeks are counted in UTC. Manual versions are never removed.
versions.daysInvalid: Use whole numbers with 1 ≤ first ≤ second ≤ 3650.
versions.waitHelp: After editing, if there is no new change for {{minutes}} minutes, a version is saved automatically.
versions.waitInvalid: Use a whole number of minutes from 1 to 60.

trash.title: Trash
trash.description: Notes moved to the trash are permanently deleted once they've been there longer than this (checked once an hour). If you shorten it, notes already past the new limit are deleted starting at the next check (up to 2,000 per check).
trash.daysInvalid: Use a whole number from 1 to 3650.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Every group on this site, with its storage use and plan.

login.description: The ways you can sign in to this site.

authorization.description: Let outside tools, such as Claude, read and write your notes as you.

mcp.title: Connect Claude with MCP
mcp.description: Hook this site up to Claude Code or Claude Desktop, in one of two ways: authorize over OAuth (no token to keep safe), or use a personal token.
mcp.oauthDescription: Nothing to create or keep safe: the client opens your browser to ask for authorization, then renews its access on its own; it lapses after {{days}} days without use. Once authorized, it shows up in the list above as an App.
mcp.oauthClaudeCode: Claude Code: run this in a terminal, then type /mcp in Claude Code, pick knotebook → Authenticate, and finish in your browser
mcp.oauthClaudeDesktop: Claude Desktop (Windows): add under mcpServers in claude_desktop_config.json
mcp.oauthDesktopNote: Needs Node.js. After saving, quit Claude Desktop completely and start it again; it opens your browser to ask for authorization (the consent page calls it “MCP CLI Proxy”).
mcp.oauthConsentNote: The first time you authorize, the permission boxes on the consent page start unticked, so pressing “{{allow}}” straight away gives read-only access; tick “{{edit}}” first if Claude should create or edit notes.
mcp.oauthHttpsOnly: Authorizing over OAuth needs an https site; this site is http, so use a personal token below.
mcp.patDescription: For scripts, or clients that don't support OAuth. Replace <YOUR_TOKEN> in the snippets with a token created above.
mcp.claudeCode: Claude Code: run in a terminal
mcp.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop: add under mcpServers in claude_desktop_config.json
mcp.windowsNote: On Windows, Claude Desktop usually needs the command wrapped in cmd /c ….
mcp.copyFailed: Couldn't copy automatically — select it by hand.
mcp.scopes: Read: list_notes, search_notes, read_note_outline, read_note_section, read_note_image, list_trash, list_folders and create_transfer_token (download). Edit adds edit_note, create_note, copy_note (into your own notes), create_folder, rename_folder, move_folder, move_note_to_folder and create_transfer_token uploads. Move is needed for move_note_to_group and copying into a group (moving into a group can't be undone, so it is a separate permission). Delete is needed for delete_note and restore_note, which move notes to the trash and back, and for delete_folder, which can move the notes in a folder to the trash; no tool here deletes a note permanently, but a note left in the trash can still be deleted permanently later, by the site's trash setting or by someone in the web app.

tokens.name: Name
tokens.label: Label
tokens.editHint: 1–32 letters, digits, . _ or -. Leave empty to go back to “{{derived}}”, derived from the name.
tokens.labelInvalid: A label can only use 1–32 letters, digits, . _ or -.
tokens.editLocked: Finish editing the other token first.
tokens.footnote: The name is where the token came from when it was created (yours for a token you made, self-reported by the client for an OAuth app) and can't be changed. The label is the short name shown on the AI's name tag and in the edit history; you can change it, and several tokens can share one.
tokens.oauthExpiryNote: An App's expiry date is {{days}} days after it was last used (or after it was authorized, if it hasn't been used yet): it renews automatically while in use, and lapses after {{days}} days without use.

storage.versionsNote: Versions and note text don't count toward storage; quotas count uploaded files only.

groups.overview: Groups you belong to, and your role in each. Create or manage groups from the sidebar.
groups.empty: You're not in any group yet.

about.description: Knotebook is a self-hosted collaborative notebook.

account.description: The name others see, and the name in your public links.

displayName.title: Display name
displayName.description: The name shown in the share panel, version history and group member lists.
displayName.label: Display name

autoVersions.title: Automatic versions
autoVersions.description: When off, your personal notes only get a new version when you save one by hand.

account.passwordLoginOffNote: This site only allows signing in through a sign-in service right now; your password is only used to prove it's you when linking an account.

setPassword.title: Add a password
setPassword.description: After adding a password you can also sign in with your email and password.
setPassword.ssoOnlyNotice: This site only allows signing in through a sign-in service right now.

account.handleDescription: The name used in your public links (/p/<handle>/…). It appears in every /n/ and /p/ link you share (token links don't include it). After a rename those links stop working immediately, and the old name is freed: anyone, including you, can take it. If someone else takes it, an old link that matches one of their notes leads to their note.

signInMethods.title: Sign-in methods
signInMethods.description: Sign-in services linked to this account. You can link another one, or unlink one as long as you keep at least one way to sign in.
signInMethods.unlinkDescription: You won't be able to sign in with it until you link it again. Other sessions stay signed in.
signInMethods.lastMethodHint: This is your only way to sign in, so it can't be unlinked.

account.apiTokensDescription: Give a script or an AI assistant access to your notes on your behalf. A token can always list and read the notes you can read; creating and writing notes needs "Create and edit notes", and moving or copying notes into groups also needs "Move or copy notes into groups". Moving notes to the trash or restoring them also needs "Move notes to the trash and restore them". Treat it like a password. Tokens are not affected when you change your password; revoke them here instead.
account.apiTokensCleanupHint: Apps past their expiry date, and tokens that expired more than 30 days ago, are usually removed automatically the next time anyone creates a token or authorizes an application; you can revoke any that are still listed yourself.
account.apiTokensScopeMove: Move or copy notes into groups
account.apiTokensScopeMoveHint: Moving a note into a group can't be undone: it removes the note's per-person shares, its public link and its version history, the group becomes its owner, and from then on the group's roles decide who can change or delete it. Every member of the group can read what is moved or copied there. Requires "Create and edit notes".
account.apiTokensScopeDelete: Move notes to the trash and restore them
account.apiTokensScopeDeleteHint: Can't delete notes permanently, but notes left in the trash can still be deleted permanently later, by the site's trash setting or by someone in the web app.
account.apiTokensOnceWarning: Copy this token now — it will not be shown again.
account.apiTokensCreateHint: Name it after whatever will use it, so you can tell tokens apart later.
account.apiTokensCopyFailed: Couldn't copy automatically — select the token above and copy it by hand.
account.apiTokensUnverifiedName: Name is self-reported by the application and is not verified.
account.apiTokensRevokeDescription: Anything using "{{name}}" will stop working immediately. This can't be undone.
account.handleInvalid: 1–32 characters: lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; hyphens can't lead, trail, or repeat.

ai.title: AI providers & actions
ai.description: Point Knotebook at your own AI endpoint, then choose which quick actions appear in the editor.
ai.baseUrlChangeClearsKey: Changing the Base URL clears the stored API key — enter it again here, or after saving.
ai.keySet: Already set — enter a new value to overwrite
ai.degradedNotice: This provider's stored key can no longer be decrypted. Enter the API key again to restore it.
ai.noKeyNotice: No API key stored — required for a hosted provider, optional for an unauthenticated local one.
ai.deleteProviderDescription: This will remove "{{name}}" and all of its models. This can't be undone.
ai.actionUserTemplateHint: Must include a {{placeholder}} placeholder for the selected text.
ai.actionUserTemplateHintInstruct: Must include {{instruction}} and {{text}}; {{focus}} is optional. The server wraps each one in fixed tags.
